page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Above it, a decorative ornament band. Title block centred: book title, then "De Triplici Methodo. CAP. I." Large decorated initial A opens the first paragraph. Page number top right. No margin notes. Signature H at the foot.

main_text.l: dè antequam de Methodo, & docendi ratio-
ne differuerimus, satis non poterit. Nam ad
Quid est Methodus? Ars quæ quemad-
modum disciplina omnis redigi in artem &
certam rationem possit, demonstrat. hoc est,
quemadmodum ex iis rebus, quarum ars non-
Quid est Ars? Antonius apud Ciceronem
lib.de Orat.II, sic definit: Ars est, quæ cogni-
tis penitusque perspectis, & in unum exitum
continetur. Aristoteles autem, Artem dicit es-
se rei per suas causas cognitionem, quæ aliter
se habere non possunt. Apud Lucianum vero

page.notes: Large decorative initial A of "ACTENUS" and ornament band at the top are decoration, not transcribed. The text is set in roman type with ligatures (ct, ff rendered as long s). The "s" in the original is transcribed as plain s. The Roman numeral "II" after "Orat." is printed with dotted-i shapes. No catchword is printed. The page ends mid-sentence, so the text continues on the next page.
